doc.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Musicians' union delay and working as a designer
summary: He worked as a designer; the Toronto local told him to wait a year for membership, so he played under-the-table gigs.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Did you employ your art degree in Toronto?

Yeah. Sure. I worked as a designer initially because in those days I had been a member of the musician’s union in Britain. In those days I didn’t know this, but I went to the Local and said I was a member of the MU and I’d come to Canada and I’d like to transfer and join the local in Toronto. And I’ll never forget the secretary/treasurer of the Local at that time was Michael Walter Murdock, another Scot, and he told me to bugger off and come back in a year.
Because you had to have a year’s residence to become a member. So of course I did play, but sort of under the table gigs.
That’s even worse than in New York, I think it was six months.
Yeah. And it’s changed now, I mean it’s much easier now I think.
He told you to bugger off, huh?
Yeah. Well actually he put it even more strongly than that.
Yeah, my jaw dropped. But just his way.
